**Fix:** set `paid_from` / `paid_to` and the account currencies by hand before `set_missing_values()`, which skips the permission path. See the note on Payment Entry creation from a Guest context.

title: A Payment Entry cannot be allocated to a Sales Order with `per_billed >= 100`; the invoice is the valid reference
content:
Once a Sales Order has `per_billed >= 100`, ERPNext refuses a Payment Entry allocated to it: `ValidationError: Sales Order SO-0001 has already been fully paid`. The receivable has moved to the Sales Invoice, which is the only valid target. A reconciler that allocated every payment to the Sales Order failed permanently for every fully invoiced order and gave up after its look-back window, stranding captured payments.

```python
per_billed = float(frappe.db.get_value("Sales Order", so_name, "per_billed") or 0)
if per_billed < 100:
    ref = ("Sales Order", so_name)
else:
    ref = ("Sales Invoice", oldest_submitted_si_with_outstanding)   # outstanding_amount > 0
```

An 'amount outstanding' helper that only sums `Payment Entry Reference` rows against the Sales Order returns the full amount for a fully invoiced order and walks into the exception; it has to consult `per_billed` and return nothing when neither document owes anything.

title: `download_pdf` returns 417 'broken image links' for every document when one file URL contains a space; print assets are cached
content:
`frappe/utils/pdf.py` catches any wkhtmltopdf `OSError` and re-raises `PDF generation failed because of broken image links`; `ContentNotFoundError` covers any failed fetch (CSS, fonts, or the renderer being unable to reach the site), so the message is a guess. In one install every document and print format returned HTTP 417 because two `/files/` URLs contained literal spaces: a Letter Head `content` field (`background: url('.../My Logo.png')`) and a Print Format `format_data` image. Both fail when fetched raw and answer 200 percent-encoded. One unfetchable resource aborts the entire render, so even `format=Standard` with `no_letterhead=1` failed until the letter head was fixed.

Rewriting the URLs to `%20` fixed it. Print formats and letterheads are cached: re-testing right after the write still returned 417, which produced a wrong 'environmental fault' write-up; every combination returned 200 minutes later with no further change. A sweep of all Letter Heads and Print Formats for URLs with spaces finds other offenders. The extra `download_pdf` parameters (`format`, `letterhead`, `settings`, `_lang`) were not required.

title: `POST /api/resource/DocType` for a submittable DocType with `amended_from` in the body creates it twice
content:
Creating a submittable DocType over REST with `amended_from` already in the JSON yields a DocType with two `amended_from` fields: Frappe's `make_amendable()` appends one for every `is_submittable` DocType, and its existence check queries the database, which cannot yet see the field in the body being inserted. A `PUT` of the same body afterwards collapses the duplicate, because by then the field exists in the DB.

Leaving `amended_from` out of the JSON is not a fix: Frappe refuses to save a submittable DocType without it, and the error does not name the field. A read-back of the field list after creation is what catches the duplicate.

title: Serial No with a NULL purchase_date causes a repost error on Item merge
content:
**Symptom:** an Item merge fails with "You cannot repost item valuation before 1900-03-31".
**Root cause:** Serial No records with `purchase_date = NULL` (stored as `0000-00-00`).
**Fix:** set `purchase_date` to the record's `creation` date on the affected Serial Nos. New Serial Nos with a null purchase_date bring the same error back.

title: 'Server was too busy to process this request' can be a `tabSeries` row lock held until commit
content:
Naming a document reads its `tabSeries` row with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` (`getseries`, called from `set_new_name()` right after Before Insert), and the row stays locked until that transaction commits or rolls back. Every other insert that uses the same series key waits behind it, and DocTypes that share a key (for example the empty-key row shared by `format:` and bare-hash names) contend site-wide. A long transaction that names documents (a bulk job creating many records in one transaction, mail ingestion creating tickets, a slow external HTTP call inside the naming request) blocks all of them. When `innodb_lock_wait_timeout` expires, the waiters get MariaDB error 1205, which Frappe treats as a timeout and returns as HTTP 508; the desk shows it as 'Server was too busy to process this request. Please try again.' CPU and workers can be idle at the time.

Raising `innodb_lock_wait_timeout` turns the error into a longer hang. A retried request can overlap the original, which may still commit, so identical inserts can be in flight together. `information_schema.innodb_trx` ordered by `trx_started` shows the transaction holding the lock.

title: `frappe.client.set_value` on a child-table field replaces every row, e.g. wiping a user's roles
content: `frappe.client.set_value` with a child-table field replaces all existing child rows. One call setting `roles` on a User wiped all of a user's roles. Passing an object as the fieldname is a related way to overwrite a table. Child tables are safer to change as a whole document (load, append or remove one row, save) or in the desk. A partial `PUT` through `/api/resource` that carries only scalar fields leaves child rows alone: updating `subject` and `message` on a Notification left all its Notification Recipient rows intact.

title: Standard Notifications refuse edits; single-brace `{doc.field}` placeholders render literally
content:
Notifications with `is_standard = 1` refuse any edit: `ValidationError: Cannot edit Standard Notification. To edit, please disable this and duplicate it`. Even if an edit went through, `bench migrate` would revert a standard record. The route is to disable the standard one and create a custom duplicate with the same document type, event and condition.

A Notification message that uses single braces (`{doc.field_name}`) renders them literally; Jinja placeholders need double braces (`{{ doc.field_name }}`). A message written this way can print the raw placeholder for months unnoticed. Several enabled Notifications can fire on the same event with identical subjects (several notifications on Sales Invoice submit), so a list of enabled notifications per document type shows overlapping or contradictory customer mail before a new sender is added.

title: A stylesheet `<link>` in an email's HTML is fetched by `frappe.sendmail`, and a 404 makes the send fail
content:
Outgoing mail HTML is inlined with Premailer, which loads every `<link rel="stylesheet">` in the message. Before that, links in the message are made absolute against the site URL, so a protocol-relative `//fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=...` becomes `<site URL>//fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=...`, which the site answers with 404. Premailer calls `raise_for_status()`, so `frappe.sendmail` raises `requests.exceptions.HTTPError` while the mail is being queued; an unreachable stylesheet host raises `ConnectionError` the same way.

Inbound HTML mail often carries such a tag (a web-font link), so a hook that sends mail containing a received Communication's content (an auto-reply, a forward, a reply that quotes it) fails on a purely cosmetic tag, and an exception raised while a received mail is processed makes the mail sync pick the message up again. Removing `<link>` tags whose text contains `stylesheet` from `doc.content` in a Before Insert Server Script on received Communications avoids it (a string scan, since `re` is unavailable in the sandbox). Communications stored with the tag earlier can still fail when replied to.

title: A Sales Order row appended with `rate: 0.0` is treated as unset and filled from the Item Price
content: `0.0` is falsy, so ERPNext's `set_missing_values` treats a `rate` of 0 as not set and fills it from the price list. A free or service line (for example a warranty item) appended with `rate: 0.0` therefore picks up any non-zero Item Price, including a stale one, and the order total is inflated by that price plus tax. Prepaid orders then show as Overdue and cash-on-delivery orders collect the inflated amount. The fix is the Item Price (set to 0) rather than the script; any new zero-priced item needs a 0 selling price in the Standard Selling price list or the surcharge recurs silently. A matcher that tests `price == 0 or "free" in title` first is a similar trap: when a second 0-priced variant is added, it falls into the first branch and gets the wrong item, so the zero-price branch is a catch-all that has to come last.
